title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'suite' of La Longue Marche (pp. 650 bis ff.). On the previous page Grothendieck builds, for N ≥ 1, an object written O_N or D̂_N. Its 'sections' are formal expressions n + N[λ] with n in Z and λ a section of a profinite-type ring scheme Ẑ_0 over a base S_0. The multiplication is (n+N[λ])(n'+N[λ']) = nn' + N[nλ' + n'λ + Nλλ'], with the relations (67 b). Note: the earlier transcription omits the factor N in the last term; it is needed for associativity and for compatibility with n + Nλ.

He then generalises. Take an associative unital Z-algebra A and a two-sided ideal J that is a free Z-module of finite type, with B = A/J. Write J̲ for the 'completed' or schematic version of J (J ⊗ Ẑ_0 over S_0). Define the commutative group scheme A̲_[N] as the pushout (70): 0 → J_{S0} → A_{S0} × J̲ → A̲_[N] → 0, with λ ↦ (λ, −λ). In other words, the constant ring A_{S0} is glued to J̲ along J. The semi-direct ('½-direct') ring structure on A_{S0} × J̲ makes the image of J an ideal (marginal cross-reference to p. 674).

This page then states:
(71) A̲_[N] is a ring scheme, sitting in an exact sequence 1 → J̲ → A̲_[N] → B_{S0} → 1, where the last map is a homomorphism of ring schemes. The quotient is the constant ring scheme B.
(72) Passing to multiplicative group functors (the 'prégroupe' or ×-group of a ring scheme, a G_m-type construction) gives 1 → (1+J̲)* → A̲_[N]* → (B_{S0})* → 1, with (B_{S0})* = (B*)_{S0}.
(73) (1+J̲)* is the subfunctor of 1+J̲ of elements invertible in A̲_[N]. As a scheme it is {(λ,λ') ∈ J̲×J̲ | λ + λ' + λλ' = 0}.
(74) For A = Z, J = NZ this specialises to 1 → (1+NẐ_0)* → O_N* → (Z/NZ)*_{S0} → 1.

The next page defines (1+NZ)* = {λ ∈ Ẑ_0 | 1+Nλ invertible}. It notes that the D̂_N form a projective system of rings, with D̂_1* = Ẑ*. It computes the kernel of D̂_N* → D̂_1* as {1+N[λ] | Nλ = 0} ≅ _NẐ_0, i.e. N-torsion.

Purpose: to produce ring and group schemes interpolating between Z (or an order A) and its completion Ẑ_0 with a level-N congruence structure. Presumably these serve the profinite/Galois-theoretic (cyclotomic, Teichmüller-tower) arithmetic of the Longue Marche, where Ẑ* acts. The construction is a fibre-product/pushout ring analogous to the classical ring Z + NẐ ⊂ Ẑ, made schematic, with a torsion phenomenon in the kernel.
errors: Exactness on the right in (72) (surjectivity on units) is asserted without justification. For general A and J it requires that units of B lift, i.e. some Henselian/radical property of J̲ inside A̲_[N]. For A = Z with J̲ = NẐ_0 it is plausible because Ẑ-elements congruent to a unit mod N can be chosen invertible. For general A it is a gap.
Description (73) via pairs with λ+λ'+λλ'=0 implicitly assumes commutativity, or two-sided inverses. For A only 'associative (disons)', one needs both λ+λ'+λλ'=0 and λ+λ'+λ'λ=0.
On the previous page, formula (68) as transcribed lacks the factor N in the λλ' term. It should read nn' + N[nλ' + n'λ + Nλλ'] for compatibility with n+Nλ. This may be a transcription issue.

ideas.what: Gluing a constant ring scheme A_{S0} to a completed ideal J̲ by a pushout, giving a ring scheme extension of B_{S0} by J̲
ideas.modern_name: fibre-product/Milnor-square type ring construction (analogue of Z + NẐ), schematic version; ring schemes over a base
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Milnor squares; ring schemes à la Greenberg/Demazure–Gabriel)

ideas.what: Multiplicative group functor of a ring scheme and the exact sequence of units 1→(1+J)*→A*→B*→1
ideas.modern_name: unit group scheme / congruence subgroup sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (units mod N, congruence subgroups); Demazure–Gabriel for ring-scheme formalism
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 treats G_m-type functors of algebras in general

ideas.what: Specialisation to O_N* → (Z/NZ)* with kernel (1+NẐ_0)*, and (next page) torsion kernel _NẐ_0 in the projective system D̂_N*
ideas.modern_name: level-N congruence structure on Ẑ*, cyclotomic-character type objects

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the projective system of ring schemes D̂_N and group schemes D̂_N*, built for any order-like pair (A, J). He explicitly declines (next page) to study its structure or its projective limits. This page gives the general framework for that system.
missed.quote: On trouve bien une structure d'anneau sur A̲_[N], et une suite exacte
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally. It is a schematic version of level structures on Ẑ*, possibly feeding the Galois/Teichmüller arithmetic of the Longue Marche. The content itself is routine algebra.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine formal construction (pushout ring scheme, unit-group exact sequence, specialisation to Z/NZ). It is interesting only as a piece of the unpublished Longue Marche continuation; no new result.
transcription_corrections: Marginal '674' above the arrow is a cross-reference to page 674, not part of the formula.
In (73) the first line should read (1+J̲)* ⊂ 1+J̲ with J̲ underlined; '1+λ inv. dans A̲' refers to the underlined (schematic) A̲.
'prégroupe [?]' is plausibly 'préfaisceau en groupes' or similar; the reading is uncertain.
Final line likely 'où le noyau ...' introducing the definition on the next page.
